name: Rebekah Horton Library
description: Main campus library, named for Dr. Rebekah L. Horton and opened in the early 1990s.

name: Academic Center
description: Large classroom building with a multimedia auditorium, labs and faculty offices, opened in 1985.

name: MacKenzie Building
description: Six-story academic building with classrooms, a banquet hall and a planetarium, named for a charter board member.

name: Administration Building
description: Campus administrative offices building completed around 1980.

name: Dale Horton Auditorium
description: Performing arts auditorium used for chapel and church services, named for the father of the college's founder.

name: Visual and Performing Arts Center
description: Music, art, speech and broadcasting facilities that includes a recital hall; formerly the Communicative Arts Center.

name: Crowne Centre
description: Large multipurpose complex with a rotating auditorium stage and two chapels.

name: Mullenix Chapel
description: Former church building, renamed in 2015, used for concerts, recitals and weddings.

name: Crawford Chapel
description: Chapel and reception space named for Dr. William Crawford and Bev Crawford.

name: Taylor Chapel
description: Chapel named for Pastor Bob Taylor.

name: Arlin R. Horton Sports Center
description: Sports complex with a basketball arena, ice rink, bowling lanes and racquetball courts, named for the college's founder.

name: John Ray Hall Field House
description: Field house named for a Pensacola Christian School board member, which hosted the college's first home games in 1981.

name: Grant Field
description: Outdoor field named for David Grant.

name: Swim Center
description: Indoor pool with shallow, racing and diving areas, opened in 1986.

name: Four Winds
description: Large dining hall with an all-you-can-eat food court and over 1,600 seats; the name reflects the international student body.

name: The Palms
description: Fast-food restaurant in the Commons area, expanded and renamed in 2016.

name: Varsity and Commons
description: Student dining and social complex that includes a dining hall, bowling alley, bookstore and post office.

name: Ballard Hall
description: Early campus building from 1974 that served several purposes before becoming a residence hall, named for Bessie Ballard.

name: Coberly Hall
description: Residence hall from the mid-1970s, named for a Pensacola businessman who chaired the charter board.

name: Griffith Tower
description: Nine-story women's residence tower built in 1981 and named for Vea Griffith.

name: Dixon Tower
description: Nine-story women's residence tower named for Doris Dixon.

name: Bradley Tower
description: Ten-story women's residence hall named for Mrs. Quirey Bradley, with soundproof piano practice rooms.

name: Young Tower
description: Men's residence hall named for William F. Young, with soundproof piano practice rooms.

name: Rice Tower
description: Eleven-story men's residence hall named for Dr. Bill Rice III, with soundproof piano practice rooms.

name: Cogeneration Plant
description: Campus power plant that supplied electricity, heating and cooling and also served as an engineering lab.

name: Campus House
description: Affordable guest hotel for families and visitors.

name: Graf Clinic
description: Campus medical clinic named for Dr. George Graf, the college's first consulting physician.

name: Campanile
description: Six-story tower at the center of campus that houses a carillon of bells.

name: Water Tower
description: Tall tank that holds about one million gallons of water to keep campus water pressure up.

name: West Campus
description: Waterfront property on Perdido Bay used for sailing, rowing and recreation.
